interest: Index of 1930s US surveillance of suspected Japanese espionage and propaganda, covering FBI/ONI probes, citizen tips, and school/church outreach.
overview: This file comprises a sequence of official U.S. Department of State Purport Lists (Lists of Papers) and docket sheets for decimal file 894.20211, documenting military activities, espionage, and propaganda conducted by Japan in the United States and adjacent regions between 1932 and 1939. The records catalog communications, investigative reports, memoranda, and diplomatic despatches exchanged between the State Department (notably the Division of Far Eastern Affairs), the War Department (Military Intelligence Division), the Navy Department (Office of Naval Intelligence), the Department of Justice (Federal Bureau of Investigation), foreign service posts, and private citizens. Major topics include surveillance of Japanese naval attachés and intelligence officers, unauthorized photography of sensitive transport and coastal defense infrastructure, intelligence operations disguised as commercial or academic enterprises, espionage networks involving foreign nationals, and Japanese propaganda efforts directed toward American educational, civic, and minority groups.
